headline: Iraq boosts oil exports via Turkey to 500,000 bpd and signs West Qurna-2 deal with Chevron amid the Hormuz war
dek: Iraq has increased oil exports to Turkey through Ceyhan from 350,000 to 500,000 barrels per day, a 43% rise and the highest volume through the route since operations resumed in September 2025 after a ~2.5-year suspension over Baghdad-Erbil revenue disputes; about 200,000 bpd of Basra crude is…
sources: Jerusalem Post report citing Shafaq News (export volumes) and the Iraqi News Agency (Chevron/West Qurna-2 minister confirmation)
fault_line: Escape route or symbolism -- does a 500,000 bpd Turkish reroute prove Iraq can survive a closed Hormuz, or is it a rounding error against Gulf-scale flows?
